query: What satisfaction and complaint themes appear in Yelp reviews?

per_column.name: sentiment_type
per_column.rationale: Positive/negative sentiment is the overarching valence of satisfaction vs complaint itself, i.e. a restatement of the whole concept's polarity rather than a specific constitutive aspect (facet) of what the satisfaction or complaint is about.

per_column.name: primary_theme
per_column.rationale: Values like food_quality, service, pricing, atmosphere, cleanliness, value, and portion_size are genuine aspects OF satisfaction/complaint -- the constitutive dimensions along which reviewers express praise or grievance. This is a real meronymic decomposition of the concept.

per_column.name: theme_count
per_column.rationale: A count of how many themes appear is a meta/structural summary statistic, not an aspect OF satisfaction or complaint. It measures the enumeration, not a part of the concept.

judge.rationale: Only one column (primary_theme) is a genuine faceted decomposition of the concept, and even it collapses multiple facets into a single 'primary' categorical rather than exposing each facet as its own aspect. sentiment_type merely restates the overall valence of the concept and thus overlaps conceptually with what the themes already encode (general_positive/general_negative buckets), hurting mutual exclusivity; theme_count is a structural meta-statistic, not a facet. Because the facet content is confined to a single column with a forced-primary constraint (and catch-all general_positive/general_negative buckets), the set does not exhaustively expose the concept's constitutive aspects as separate MECE facets.
